title: DINO: DETR with Improved DeNoising Anchor Boxes for End-to-End Object Detection

problem.summary: Even after DAB-DETR and DN-DETR, DETR-like detectors still trail the best improved classical detectors on COCO, train slowly with poorly understood queries, and had never been studied when scaled to large backbones and large-scale pre-training data.
statements: DETR-like models lag behind highly optimized classical detectors such as HTC++ and DyHead; the best of them were still under 50 AP on COCO.
DETR training convergence is slow and the meaning of its queries is unclear.
Standard denoising cannot predict 'no object' for anchors that have no ground-truth box nearby, allowing duplicate predictions when several anchors are close to one object.
DETR-like models had no reported results when scaled to a large backbone and a large-scale data set.

evidence.quote: Despite its promising performance, the training convergence of DETR is slow and the meaning of queries is unclear.
For instance, the best performing DETR-like models nowadays are still under 50 AP on COCO.
The scalability of DETR-like models has not been well studied.
However, it lacks a capability of predicting “no object” for anchors with no object nearby. To address this issue, we propose a Contrastive DeNoising (CDN) approach to rejecting useless anchors.

background.summary: DINO builds on DAB-DETR (anchor-box queries), DN-DETR (denoising training) and Deformable DETR (deformable attention, query selection, look forward once), and compares against the large-scale pre-training line of classical detectors (HTC++, DyHead, SwinV2, Florence), claiming the gap is that DETR-like models were both less accurate and untested at scale.

relatedWork.name: DN-DETR
relatedWork.relation: direct base: denoising training that stabilizes bipartite matching
relatedWork.quote: DN-DETR [17] introduces a denoising training method to speed up DETR training. It feeds noise-added ground-truth labels and boxes into the decoder and trains the model to reconstruct the original ones.

relatedWork.name: DAB-DETR
relatedWork.relation: base that formulates queries as dynamic 4D anchor boxes
relatedWork.quote: DAB-DETR [21] further extends 2D anchor points to 4D anchor box coordinates to represent queries and dynamically update boxes in each decoder layer.

relatedWork.name: Deformable DETR
relatedWork.relation: source of deformable attention, query selection and iterative box refinement
relatedWork.quote: Deformable DETR [41] predicts 2D anchor points and designs a deformable attention module that only attends to certain sampling points around a reference point.

relatedWork.name: HTC++ and DyHead
relatedWork.relation: best classical detectors that set the state of the art DINO aims to surpass
relatedWork.quote: The best detection models nowadays are based on improved classical detectors like DyHead [8] and HTC [4].

relatedWork.name: Classical detectors (Faster R-CNN line)
relatedWork.relation: prior art that relies on hand-designed components and cannot be end-to-end optimized
relatedWork.quote: Moreover, they need hand-designed components like NMS to remove duplicate boxes, and hence cannot perform end-to-end optimization.

evidence.quote: Our work of DINO in this paper is based on DAB-DETR and DN-DETR, and also adopts deformable attention for its computational efficiency.
Two main reasons contribute to the phenomenon: 1) Previous DETR-like models are inferior to the improved classical detectors.

solution.summary: DINO is an end-to-end DETR-like detector that adds three mechanisms on top of DN-DETR/DAB-DETR/Deformable DETR: contrastive denoising (CDN) with positive and hard-negative queries, mixed query selection that initializes only positional queries from top-K encoder features, and a look forward twice scheme that propagates box-refinement gradients into earlier decoder layers.
solution.approach: Train dynamic anchor-box queries with contrastive denoising (positives must reconstruct their box, negatives must predict background), initialize positional queries from encoder top-K features while keeping content queries learnable, and update each layer's boxes with gradients from the next layer.
components: Contrastive DeNoising (CDN) with inner-square positive and outer-ring negative noised queries
mixed query selection: top-K encoder features initialize positional queries only, content queries stay learnable
look forward twice box refinement (gradients from layer i+1 reach layer i)
deformable attention with multi-scale (4- and 5-scale) features
dynamic DN groups that fix the number of DN queries per image
shared prediction heads and 900 decoder queries

evidence.quote: we propose a contrastive denoising training by adding both positive and negative samples of the same ground truth at the same time.
The contrastive denoising training helps the model to avoid duplicate outputs of the same target.
we only initialize anchor boxes using the position information associated with the selected top-K features, but leave the content queries static as before.
we propose another way called look forward twice to perform box update, where the parameters of layer-i are influenced by losses of both layer-i and layer-(i + 1), as shown in Fig. 6 (b).
It helps the model to use better positional information to pool more comprehensive content features from the encoder.

experiments.summary: DINO is evaluated on COCO 2017 (val2017 and test-dev) with AP, in the 12/24/36-epoch settings with a ResNet-50 backbone and after Objects365 pre-training with SwinL, against convolutional and DETR-like baselines, plus ablations over query selection, CDN, look forward twice, layer counts and denoising-query counts.

evidence.quote: DINO achieves 49.4AP in 12 epochs and 51.3AP in 24 epochs on COCO with a ResNet-50 backbone and multi-scale features, yielding a significant improvement of +6.0AP and +2.7AP, respectively, compared to DN-DETR, the previous best DETR-like model.
after pre-training on the Objects365 dataset with a SwinL backbone, DINO obtains the best results on both COCO val2017 (63.2AP) and test-dev (63.3AP).
Moreover, our method performs especially well for small objects, gaining +7.2 AP with 4 scales and +7.5 AP with 5 scales.
It is the first time that an end-to-end Transformer detector is established as a SOTA model on the leaderboard [1].

limitations.summary: The paper has no dedicated limitations section; it does report that test-time augmentation brings no inspiring gain, that adding denoising queries beyond 100 gives little or negative returns, and that accuracy degrades sharply when decoder layers are removed.
items: Test-time augmentation did not yield an inspiring gain over traditional detectors.
Increasing the number of denoising queries beyond 100 gives only a small or even worse improvement.
Accuracy is sensitive to decoder depth: removing decoder layers hurts performance more than removing encoder layers.
The headline 63.2/63.3 AP results rely on Objects365 pre-training and a SwinL backbone rather than COCO alone.
Conditional queries from DAB-DETR did not suit the model and were dropped.

evidence.quote: Our TTA does not obtain an inspiring gain compared with traditional detectors, but we hope our exploration may provide some insights for future studies.
However, continuing to increase the DN number after 100 yields only a small additional or even worse performance improvement.
decreasing the number of decoder layers hurts the performance more significantly

futureDirections.direction: Further study of test-time augmentation for DETR-like models, where the authors' one-to-one ensembling exploration gave limited gains.
futureDirections.quote: Our TTA does not obtain an inspiring gain compared with traditional detectors, but we hope our exploration may provide some insights for future studies.

deploymentClaims: DINO-4scale runs at 24 FPS with 47M parameters and 279 GFLOPS on an A100 GPU (Table 1), with all models benchmarked on the same GPU.
DINO cuts model size and pre-training data size relative to leaderboard competitors while improving accuracy (1/15 the parameters of SwinV2-G, 1/60 the backbone pre-training images of Florence).

evidence.quote: For a fair comparison, we report both GFLOPS and FPS tested on the same A100 NVIDIA GPU for all the models listed in Table 1.
Compared to other models on the leaderboard, DINO significantly reduces its model size and pre-training data size while achieving better results.
We provide the GPU memory and training time for our base model in Table 5. All results are reported on 8 Nvidia A100 GPUs with ResNet-50 [14].
